Moreover, this Rabbi Salomon (as has been touched on) says that the Assuerus or Artaxerxes to whom this letter was written was the Assuerus who took Esther herself to wife[[Esth 2:17||]]: who, it is agreed, was not Cyrus, who gave the Jews leave to return. And a little further on this error will be refuted more clearly. [[4:12|which they are building, setting up the ramparts thereof and repairing the walls|Quam ædificant exstruentes muros ejus et parietes componentes]]. On this someone writes: “In this they accused the Jews falsely, since they were not rebuilding the city, but only the temple.” This saying cannot stand: on the contrary, they began to rebuild the city before the temple; otherwise where would they have lived? Nor would those princes have dared to write to their king a lie so manifest and so open to the eye. Cyrus too gave the Jews leave to rebuild not only the temple but also the city, as will soon be proved.

paras.t: Nunc ergo notum sit regi, quia si civitas illa ædificata fuerit, et muri ejus instaurati, tributum et vectigal et annuos reditus non dabunt, id est, tibi erunt rebelles, renuendo persolvere reditus, quos omni anno solvere obligantur de terræ nascentibus et arborum fructibus, tributa quoque et vectigalia. Dicitur autem tributum, quod datur seu solvitur ministro principis deputato ad levandum hujusmodi bonum; vectigal autem, quod principi apportatur, seu pedagium quod solvitur de rebus quæ vehuntur per terram aut aquas. Et usque ad reges hæc noxa, id est rebellio et offensio ista, perveniet, id est usque ad te, successoresque tuos. Nos autem memores salis quod in palatio comedimus, id est, ad memoriam revocantes beneficia collata nobis a te et a patribus tuis usque ad minima, scilicet usque ad sal, vel usque ad cibos sale conditos, nuntiamus regi, ut recenseas, id est, recolas et inquiri facias, in libris historiarum patrum tuorum; et invenies scriptum in commentariis, et scies quia urbs illa, urbs rebellis est.
paras.en: [[4:13|And now be it known to the king, that if this city be built up, and the walls thereof repaired|Nunc ergo notum sit regi, quia si civitas illa ædificata fuerit, et muri ejus instaurati]], [[4:13|they will not pay tribute nor toll, nor yearly revenues|tributum et vectigal et annuos reditus non dabunt]]: that is, they will be rebels against thee, refusing to pay the revenues which they are bound to pay every year from the produce of the land and the fruits of the trees, and the tributes and tolls as well. Now *tribute* is what is given or paid to the prince's officer appointed to levy goods of this kind; *toll* [*vectigal*] what is brought to the prince, or the duty paid on goods carried by land or by water. [[4:13|and this loss|Et usque ad reges hæc noxa]], that is, this rebellion and offence, [[4:13|will fall upon the kings|perveniet]], that is, upon thee and thy successors. [[4:14|But we remembering the salt that we have eaten in the palace|Nos autem memores salis quod in palatio comedimus]], that is, calling to mind the benefits conferred on us by thee and by thy fathers down to the least of them, namely down to salt, or down to food seasoned with salt, [[4:14|certified the king|nuntiamus regi]] [Denis reads *nuntiamus*, “we certify”], [[4:15|That search may be made|ut recenseas]], that is, that thou mayest recall it and have inquiry made, [[4:15|in the books of the histories of thy fathers|in libris historiarum patrum tuorum]]; [[4:15|and thou shalt find written in the records|et invenies scriptum in commentariis]], [[4:15|and shalt know that this city is a rebellious city|et scies quia urbs illa, urbs rebellis est]].

paras.t: Sequitur responsio regis. Verbum, id est responsivam epistolam, misit rex ad Reum, id est ipsi Reum ac ceteris qui cum eo scripserant regi. A me præceptum est, et recensuerunt scribæ mei in libris historiarum, inveneruntque, quoniam civitas illa ab antiquis diebus adversus reges rebellat, id est, rebellare consuevit. Et hoc reges et cives Jerusalem quandoque fecerunt juste, ut patet de David, Asa, Josaphat, Ezechia; quandoque injuste, ut tempore Joakim et Sedeciæ, quando Deus propter peccata eorum subdidit eos infidelium regibus. Nam et reges fortissimi fuerunt in Jerusalem, qui dominati sunt omni regioni quæ trans fluvium est; prout secundo et tertio Regum de David et Salomone refertur. Tributum quoque et vectigal et reditus accipiebant, id est, reges illi Jerusalem, scilicet David, Salomon, receperunt tributa et alia quæque a regnis et provinciis, scilicet Syria, Moab, Ammon, Idumæa, quas sibi subjecerant. Nunc ergo audite sententiam: Prohibeatis viros illos ab exsecutione ædificationis, ut urbs illa non ædificetur.
paras.en: There follows the king's answer. [[4:17|The king sent word|Verbum, id est responsivam epistolam, misit rex]] (*word*, that is, a letter in answer) [[4:17|to Reum|ad Reum]], that is, to Reum himself and the others who had written to the king with him. [[4:19|And I commanded|A me præceptum est]]: [[4:19|and search hath been made|et recensuerunt]] by my scribes in the books of the histories, [[4:19|and it is found, that this city|inveneruntque, quoniam civitas illa]] [[4:19|of old time hath rebelled against kings|ab antiquis diebus adversus reges rebellat]], that is, has been wont to rebel. And this the kings and citizens of Jerusalem sometimes did justly, as is plain of David[[2 Kings 8:1||]], Asa, Josaphat[[2 Par 20:1||]] and Ezechias[[4 Kings 18:7||]]; sometimes unjustly, as in the time of Joakim[[4 Kings 24:1||]] and Sedecias[[4 Kings 24:20||]] [the margin notes beside this passage are largely illegible; these references are given from the events Denis names], when God for their sins subjected them to the kings of unbelievers. [[4:20|For there have been powerful kings in Jerusalem|Nam et reges fortissimi fuerunt in Jerusalem]], [[4:20|who have had dominion over all the country that is beyond the river|qui dominati sunt omni regioni quæ trans fluvium est]]; as is related in the second and third books of Kings of David[[2 Kings 8:6||]] and Solomon[[3 Kings 4:21||]]. [[4:20|and have received tribute, and toll and revenues|Tributum quoque et vectigal et reditus accipiebant]]: that is, those kings of Jerusalem, namely David and Solomon, received tributes and everything else from the kingdoms and provinces which they had subjected to themselves, namely Syria, Moab, Ammon and Idumæa. [[4:21|Now therefore hear the sentence|Nunc ergo audite sententiam]]: [[4:21|Hinder those men|Prohibeatis viros illos]] from carrying out the building, [[4:21|that this city be not built|ut urbs illa non ædificetur]] [the end of this lemma is illegible in the OCR and is supplied from the Vulgate].

paras.t: Circa hoc scribit quidam: Ex quo patet, quod Artaxerxes iste fuit Cyrus, et non retractavit edictum suum: quia non dederat licentiam ædificandi civitatem, sed tantum templum, ut habetur supra, nec istud retractavit. Circa hoc dico, quod Artaxerxes iste non fuit Cyrus, qui dedit licentiam ædificandi templum, sicut dictum est et probatum, quia secundum Hieronymum in multis locis expositionum suarum super Prophetas, Cyrus ille fuit omnino per omnia favorabilis ipsis Judæis: et hoc Beda, Haymo et ceteri Catholici concorditer dicunt. Insuper, falsum est et sacræ Scripturæ contrarium, dicere quod Cyrus iste non dedit Judæis licentiam reædificandi civitatem, sed solum templum: quoniam (ut in expositione superiori allegatum est plenius) de Cyro hoc rege Persarum per Isaiam Dominus prænuntiavit: Ipse ædificabit civitatem meam. Quod certum est de urbe Jerusalem esse prædictum, et esse sensum: Ipse ædificabit, id est ædificari licentiabit et permittet, aut certe jubebit: secundum quod ipsemet Cyrus dixit: Ipse, scilicet Deus cæli, præcepit mihi ut ædificarem ei domum in Jerusalem. Si ergo Cyrus prohibuit civitatem ædificari, suum utique edictum revocavit. Nec verum est primo haberi capitulo hujus libri, quod Cyrus dedit Judæis licentiam reædificandi solum templum. Nam quamvis ibi dicatur de templo construendo, non tamen additur ibi aliquid de præcisione aut exclusione aliorum. Iterum, dictum est Cyrum fuisse inductum ad templi reparationem, quia Hebræi ostenderunt ei præfatam Isaiæ prophetiam. Et quia in ea de civitatis reædificatione manifeste habetur, constat quod ad hoc dedit licentiam: imo de civitatis reædificatione habetur ibi apertius quam de templi constructione, ut patet ex primo articulo. Rursus, Josephus undecimo Antiquitatum libro recitat Cyrum scripsisse: Judæos terram meam inhabitantes, qui voluerunt ad patriam suam redire, permisi et civitatem renovare, templumque Dei in ea ædificare. At vero, secundum opinionem illam erroneam, Cyrus suum retractasset edictum de templi ædificatione: alioqui Judæi non omisissent prosequi ædificium templi, nisi epistola regis hoc continuisset.
paras.en: On this someone writes: “From this it is plain that this Artaxerxes was Cyrus, and that he did not retract his edict: for he had not given leave to build the city, but only the temple, as we have above[[1 Esd 1:3||]], and that he did not retract.” On this I say that this Artaxerxes was not Cyrus, who gave leave to build the temple, as has been said and proved; for according to Jerome in many places of his expositions on the Prophets, that Cyrus was altogether and in everything favourable to the Jews; and Bede, Haymo and the other Catholics say this with one accord. Moreover it is false, and contrary to holy Scripture, to say that this Cyrus did not give the Jews leave to rebuild the city, but only the temple: since (as was cited more fully in the exposition above) the Lord foretold of this Cyrus king of the Persians by Isaias: [[Is 45:13|he shall build my city|Ipse ædificabit civitatem meam]][[Is 44:28||]]. It is certain that this was foretold of the city of Jerusalem, and that the sense is: *he shall build*, that is, he shall license and permit it to be built, or indeed shall command it; according to what Cyrus himself said of the God of heaven: [[1 Esd 1:2|he hath charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem|Ipse, scilicet Deus cæli, præcepit mihi ut ædificarem ei domum in Jerusalem]]. If then Cyrus forbade the city to be built, he certainly revoked his own edict. Nor is it true that the first chapter of this book has it that Cyrus gave the Jews leave to rebuild the temple only. For though it speaks there of building the temple, nothing is added there about cutting off or excluding other things. Again, it has been said that Cyrus was led to repair the temple because the Hebrews showed him the aforesaid prophecy of Isaias. And since the rebuilding of the city is plainly contained in it, it is clear that he gave leave for this; indeed the rebuilding of the city is there more openly than the building of the temple, as is plain from the first article. Once more, Josephus in the eleventh book of the Antiquities records that Cyrus wrote: “The Jews dwelling in my land who wished to return to their own country I have permitted both to renew the city and to build the temple of God in it.” But according to that erroneous opinion, Cyrus would have retracted his edict about building the temple: otherwise the Jews would not have left off carrying on the building of the temple, unless the king's letter had contained this.

paras.t: Tunc intermissum est opus domus Domini in Jerusalem, id est prosecutio templi et ædificatio civitatis, et non fiebat usque ad annum secundum regni Darii regis Persarum: qui Darius, secundum Josephum, Hieronymum et sanctos doctores, fuit filius Hystaspis et diu præcessit Assuerum, cujus conjux exstitit Esther. Aliqui vero Hebræi affirmant, quod fuit filius Assueri et Esther.
paras.en: [[4:24|Then the work of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was interrupted|Tunc intermissum est opus domus Domini in Jerusalem]], that is, the carrying on of the temple and the building of the city, [[4:24|and ceased till the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians|et non fiebat usque ad annum secundum regni Darii regis Persarum]]: which Darius, according to Josephus, Jerome and the holy doctors, was the son of Hystaspes, and came long before the Assuerus whose wife Esther was. But some Hebrews affirm that he was the son of Assuerus and Esther.

paras.t: Postremo, juxta mysticum sensum, per reædificationem templi et civitatis Jerusalem, designatur reformatio Ecclesiæ in capitibus ejus et membris. Per gentes vero impedientes, signantur invisibiles atque visibiles Ecclesiæ hostes, falsi fratres, vitiosi prælati, et omnes qui adversantur unitati, paci et reformationi Ecclesiæ: qui dum nec ratione nec auctoritate queunt Catholicis prævalere, libenter se muniunt sæcularium principum favore ac potestate, apud quos mendaciter criminantur atque accusant Catholicos; et sicut fideles, exsultant et voce altisona laudant Deum, dum Ecclesia aliqualiter reformatur. Sapientiores tamen et perfectiores, considerantes in quanta sanctitate et justitia Ecclesia Deo servivit tempore Apostolorum et postea diu, plorant dum moderni temporis qualemcumque reformationem conspiciunt.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the mystical sense, by the rebuilding of the temple and the city of Jerusalem is signified the reform of the Church in her heads and her members. By the nations that hinder it are signified the invisible and visible enemies of the Church, false brethren, vicious prelates, and all who oppose the unity, peace and reform of the Church: who, when they cannot prevail against the Catholics by reason or by authority, gladly arm themselves with the favour and power of secular princes, before whom they lyingly charge and accuse the Catholics. And as the faithful exult and praise God with a loud voice when the Church is in some measure reformed, yet the wiser and more perfect, considering in how great holiness and justice the Church served God in the time of the Apostles and long after, weep when they behold the reform, such as it is, of the present time[[1 Esd 3:12||]] [the margin note here is illegible; the allusion is to the rejoicing and weeping of 1 Esdras 3:11–12].

5.title: Explanatio capituli quinti: Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: Now Aggeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesied

paras.t: Hic agitur de resumptione ædificationis templi, et de appellatione propter hoc facta ad Darium regem.
paras.en: Here the resumption of the building of the temple is treated, and the appeal made on that account to king Darius.

paras.t: Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo, prophetantes ad Judæos qui erant in Judæa et Jerusalem, in nomine Dei Israel. Isti duo fuerunt in terra Babyloniæ nati, et inter duodecim minores computantur Prophetas. Unde in Scholastica fertur historia: Ascensuri ex Babylonia in Judæam, alios hortabantur Judæos ut secum ascenderent, sed paucos invenerunt qui assentirent eis. Propterea in exhortatione et apparatu tres annos compleverunt, et in tertio anno regni Cyri egressi sunt sub Zorobabel duce eorum et Jesu pontifice, exhortantibus eos Zacharia propheta et Aggæo juvene, sed nondum propheta. Denique, mortuo Cambyse et Dario imperante, hi duo Prophetæ admonuerunt ipsum Zorobabel atque pontificem et populum, ut rursus inciperent prosequi ædificium templi et civitatis, etiam nondum ad hoc licentia obtenta a Dario, prædicentes ex revelatione divina, quod prosperaretur opus in manu eorum, nec Darius impediret.
paras.en: [[5:1|Now Aggeus the prophet, and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesied to the Jews that were in Judea and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel.|Prophetaverunt autem Aggæus propheta et Zacharias filius Addo, prophetantes ad Judæos qui erant in Judæa et Jerusalem, in nomine Dei Israel]] These two were born in the land of Babylonia, and are counted among the twelve minor Prophets. Hence it is related in the Scholastic History: When they were about to go up from Babylonia into Judea, they urged the other Jews to go up with them, but found few who would agree with them. Therefore they spent three years in exhorting and in making ready, and in the third year of the reign of Cyrus they went out under Zorobabel their leader and Jesus the high priest, Zacharias the prophet exhorting them, and Aggeus, a young man but not yet a prophet. At length, when Cambyses was dead and Darius reigned, these two Prophets admonished Zorobabel himself, and the high priest, and the people, to begin again to carry on the building of the temple and of the city, even though leave for it had not yet been obtained from Darius, foretelling by divine revelation that the work would prosper in their hands, and that Darius would not hinder it.

paras.t: Verumtamen, secundum Josephum, Zorobabel audita promotione Darii in regem, festinanter eum accessit, quia jamdudum habuit familiarem amicitiam secum, atque (ut legitur) ex instigatione ipsius Zorobabel Darius fecit votum Deo Israel, quod si fieret rex, reædificaret civitatem Jerusalem et templum in ea. Concessit itaque Darius ipsi Zorobabel largam licentiam instaurandi templum et urbem, et privilegia multa. Sed sicut Magister in historiis scribit, iste accessus Zorobabel ad Darium, fuit postquam resumpsit ædificationem, dum principes Darii habitantes trans flumen petierunt a Zorobabel, qua auctoritate prosequeretur ædificationem dudum prohibitam, sicut jam ex textu patebit.
paras.en: However, according to Josephus, Zorobabel, on hearing that Darius had been raised to the throne, went to him in haste, because he had long had a close friendship with him; and (as we read) at the prompting of Zorobabel himself Darius had made a vow to the God of Israel that, if he became king, he would rebuild the city of Jerusalem and the temple in it. So Darius granted Zorobabel ample leave to restore the temple and the city, and many privileges. But, as the Master [that is, Peter Comestor, the "Master of the Histories"] writes in the Histories, this going of Zorobabel to Darius was after he had taken up the building again, when the princes of Darius who dwelt beyond the river demanded of Zorobabel by what authority he was carrying on a building that had long been forbidden, as will now appear from the text.

paras.t: In ipso tempore venit ad eos, id est ad Zorobabel et Judæos, Thathanai, qui erat dux trans flumen Euphraten, et Stharbusanai et consiliarii eorum, et dixerunt: Quis dedit vobis consilium, ut domum hanc ædificaretis, et muros ejus, civitatis aut templi, instauraretis? Ad quod respondimus eis, quæ essent nomina hominum auctorum illius ædificationis, id est, qui essent principales in opere illo: quod scilicet Aggæus et Zacharias ex divina revelatione hoc insinuarent esse agendum, et quod Zorobabel dudum amicus Darii, esset exsecutor operis hujus.
paras.en: [[5:3|And at the same time came to them|In ipso tempore venit ad eos]], that is, to Zorobabel and the Jews, [[5:3|Thathanai, who was governor beyond the river|Thathanai, qui erat dux trans flumen]] Euphrates, [[5:3|and Stharbuzanai, and their counsellors|et Stharbusanai et consiliarii eorum]]: [[5:3|and said|et dixerunt]]: [[5:3|Who hath given you counsel to build this house, and to repair the walls thereof|Quis dedit vobis consilium, ut domum hanc ædificaretis, et muros ejus]], of the city or of the temple? [[5:4|In answer to which we gave them the names of the men who were the promoters of|Ad quod respondimus eis, quæ essent nomina hominum auctorum]] [[5:4|that building|illius ædificationis]], that is, who were the chief in that work: namely, that Aggeus and Zacharias made known by divine revelation that this was to be done, and that Zorobabel, long a friend of Darius, was the one carrying out this work.

paras.t: Oculus autem Dei eorum, id est respectus divinæ pietatis et confortationis, factus est super senes Judæorum, eos corroborans, ita quod non cessaverunt ab incepto, et non potuerunt principes præfati inhibere eos, quia Judæi de ipsorum inhibitione non curaverunt. Vel quamvis venerunt cum inhibendi proposito, Omnipotens tamen immutavit corda eorum, ita quod non prohibuerunt. Prima tamen expositio aptior reputatur. Nam subditur: Placuitque utrique parti, puta Judæis et Samaritis, ut res ad Darium referretur, id est, causa ista ad judicium Darii regis deportaretur, quia tunc erat monarcha in oriente; et tunc satisfacerent adversus accusationem illam, id est, Judæi ex determinatione Darii responderent ad accusationem eis objectam, quod incaute haberent se, ædificando sic sine licentia regis.
paras.en: [[5:5|But the eye of their God|Oculus autem Dei eorum]], that is, the regard of the divine goodness and strengthening, [[5:5|was upon the ancients of the Jews|factus est super senes Judæorum]], strengthening them, so that they did not cease from what they had begun, [[5:5|and they could not hinder them|et non potuerunt principes præfati inhibere eos]], that is, the aforesaid princes could not, because the Jews paid no heed to their forbidding. Or: although they came with the purpose of hindering them, the Almighty nevertheless changed their hearts, so that they did not forbid them. The first exposition, however, is thought the more fitting. For it is added: [[5:5|And it was agreed|Placuitque]] by both parties, namely the Jews and the Samaritans, [[5:5|that the matter should be referred to Darius|ut res ad Darium referretur]], that is, that this case should be carried to the judgment of king Darius, because he was then monarch in the East; [[5:5|and then they should give satisfaction concerning that accusation|et tunc satisfacerent adversus accusationem illam]], that is, that the Jews, by the decision of Darius, should answer the accusation laid against them, that they were behaving rashly in building thus without the king's leave.

paras.t: Exemplar epistolæ quam misit Thathanai ad Darium, id est, sermo epistolæ quam miserant ei hi, qui cum ipso Thathanai scripserunt Dario regi, cui scripserunt sic: Dario regi pax omnis, id est pax perfecta, seu pax interior, exterior, præsens et futura. Notum sit regi, isse, id est ivisse, nos ad Judæam ad domum Dei magni. Isti enim Samaritani cum diis suis colebant et Deum Israel, quem magnum et summum esse credebant. Quæ ædificatur lapide impolito, id est ex impolitis seu non sculptis lapidibus, et ligna ponuntur in parietibus; opusque illud diligenter exstruitur, crescitque in manibus eorum.
paras.en: [[5:6|The copy of the letter that Thathanai|Exemplar epistolæ quam misit Thathanai]] sent [[5:6|to Darius|ad Darium]], that is, [[5:7|The letter which they sent him|sermo epistolæ quam miserant ei]], those who wrote to king Darius together with Thathanai himself, to whom they wrote thus: [[5:7|To Darius the king all peace|Dario regi pax omnis]], that is, perfect peace, or peace within and without, present and to come. [[5:8|Be it known to the king, that we went|Notum sit regi, isse]], that is, *ivisse* [the fuller form of the same word, "to have gone"], [[5:8|to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God|nos ad Judæam ad domum Dei magni]]. For these Samaritans worshipped the God of Israel too, together with their own gods[[4 Kings 17:33||]][[4 Kings 17:41||]], and believed him to be great and supreme. [[5:8|which they are building with unpolished stones|Quæ ædificatur lapide impolito]], that is, of rough or uncarved stones, [[5:8|and timber is laid in the walls|et ligna ponuntur in parietibus]]: [[5:8|and this work is carried on diligently and advanceth in their hands|opusque illud diligenter exstruitur, crescitque in manibus eorum]].

paras.t: Interrogavimus ergo senes illos: Quis dedit vobis potestatem, ut domum hanc ædificaretis? Responderunt: Nos sumus servi Dei cæli et terræ, et ædificamus templum quod erat exstructum ante hos annos multos, id est, ædificamus templum simile templo olim a Salomone constructo.
paras.en: [[5:9|And we asked those ancients|Interrogavimus ergo senes illos]]: [[5:9|Who hath given you authority to build this house|Quis dedit vobis potestatem, ut domum hanc ædificaretis?]]? They answered: [[5:11|We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building a temple that was built these many years ago|Nos sumus servi Dei cæli et terræ, et ædificamus templum quod erat exstructum ante hos annos multos]], that is, we are building a temple like the temple built long ago by Solomon.

paras.t: Itaque ex eo tempore quo fundamenta templi sunt a Zorobabel seu Sassabasar posita usque nunc, ædificabatur templum, non continue, sed interveniente longa interruptione ex Cambysis prohibitione, ut patuit capitulo præcedente.
paras.en: And so [[5:16|from that time|ex eo tempore]] when the foundations of the temple were laid by Zorobabel, or Sassabasar, [[5:16|until now|usque nunc]] the temple was in building, not without a break, but with a long interruption coming between, through the prohibition of Cambyses, as was shown in the preceding chapter[[1 Esd 4:21||]][[1 Esd 4:24||]].

paras.t: Nunc ergo si videtur regi bonum, recenseat in bibliotheca regis, id est in armario seu repositorio librorum suorum annalium et historialium, quæ bibliotheca est in Babylone, id est in terra Babyloniæ: siquidem urbs Babylon fuit destructa; utrumnam a Cyro rege jussum sit ut ædificaretur domus Dei in Jerusalem, et voluntatem regis super hac re mittat ad nos.
paras.en: [[5:17|Now therefore if it seem good to the king, let him search in the king's library|Nunc ergo si videtur regi bonum, recenseat in bibliotheca regis]], that is, in the press or store-room of his books of annals and histories, [[5:17|which is in Babylon|quæ bibliotheca est in Babylone]], that is, in the land of Babylonia, since the city of Babylon had been destroyed; [[5:17|whether it hath been decreed by Cyrus the king, that the house of God in Jerusalem should be built|utrumnam a Cyro rege jussum sit ut ædificaretur domus Dei in Jerusalem]], [[5:17|and let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter|et voluntatem regis super hac re mittat ad nos]].

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Tunc Darius rex præcepit, et recensuerunt in bibliotheca
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Then king Darius gave orders, and they searched in the library

paras.t: Præceptum Darii de templo ædificando et consummando, hic ponitur.
paras.en: Here is set down the command of Darius for the building and completing of the temple.

paras.t: Tunc Darius rex præcepit ministris et scriptoribus suis, et recensuerunt, id est inquisierunt, in bibliotheca librorum continentium gesta præcedentium regum, qui erant in Babylone, id est in regno Babylonis, prout se ante extenderat et includebat multa et magna regna; et inventum est in Ecbatanis, quod est castrum. In libro Judith habetur, quod Ecbatanis fuit potentissima civitas: quomodo ergo vocatur castrum? Forsan, quoniam instar fortalitii fuit firmissime facta, sicut secundum quorumdam expositionem Christus de Jerusalem dixit discipulis: Ite in castellum quod contra vos est. Vel forte Ecbatanis sumitur hic pro castro, non pro civitate. In Medena provincia, id est in regno Mediæ seu Medorum, inventum est ibi volumen unum, talisque in eo scriptus erat commentarius, id est tractatus expositorius rei gestæ per Cyrum.
paras.en: [[6:1|Then king Darius gave orders|Tunc Darius rex præcepit]] to his ministers and scribes, [[6:1|and they searched|et recensuerunt]], that is, made inquiry, [[6:1|in the library of the books|in bibliotheca librorum]] that contained the deeds of the former kings, [[6:1|that were laid up in Babylon|qui erant in Babylone]], that is, in the kingdom of Babylon, as it had formerly stretched out and taken in many great kingdoms; [[6:2|And there was found in Ecbatana, which is a castle|et inventum est in Ecbatanis, quod est castrum]]. In the book of Judith we read that Ecbatana was a most powerful city[[Jdt 1:1||]]: how then is it called a castle? Perhaps because it was made very strong, like a fortress; as, according to some men's explanation, Christ said to his disciples of Jerusalem: [[Matt 21:2|Go ye into the village that is over against you|Ite in castellum quod contra vos est]][[Mark 11:2||]] [*castellum*, literally "a castle" or "fortified place", where the Douay-Rheims has "village"]. Or perhaps Ecbatana is taken here for a castle, not for the city. [[6:2|in the province of Media|In Medena provincia]], that is, in the kingdom of Media or of the Medes, there was found [[6:2|a book|volumen unum]], [[6:2|in which this record was written|talisque in eo scriptus erat commentarius]], *record* [*commentarius*], that is, an expository account of what was done by Cyrus.

paras.t: Anno primo Cyri regis, Cyrus rex decrevit ut domus Dei quæ est, id est, esse debet, vel cujus locus est, in Jerusalem, ædificaretur in loco ubi immolent hostias, et ut ponant fundamenta supportantia altitudinem, id est structuram templi, quod erit in altitudine sexaginta cubitorum, et latitudinem cubitorum sexaginta. Aliqui opinantur, quod latitudo sumatur improprie hic pro longitudine templi, præsertim quum latitudo templi Salomonis non fuerit nisi cubitorum viginti. Verumtamen Josephus etiam refert sicut in textu habetur. Et ordines de lapidibus impolitis tres, et sic ordines de lignis novis. Hoc videtur ex verbis Josephi quasi exponi, dum ait: Et faciant tres parietes lapideos ipsius, videlicet templi, et unum parietem ligneum ex materiis ipsius provinciæ. Præterea objici potest, quia si templum istud secundum, fuit altitudinis sexaginta cubitorum, videtur fuisse altius templo Salomonis, quod habuit triginta cubitos in altitudine, prout tertio libro Regum habetur. Et respondendum, quod templum Salomonis fuit triginta cubitorum in altitudine usque ad primum tabulatum, deinde totidem usque ad tabulatum secundum, et ab illo usque ad verticem habuit adhuc in altitudine cubitos sexaginta. Unde tota ejus altitudo describitur secundo libro Paralipomenon ubi habetur: Porro altitudo centum viginti cubitorum erat.
paras.en: [[6:3|In the first year of Cyrus the king: Cyrus the king decreed, that the house of God|Anno primo Cyri regis, Cyrus rex decrevit ut domus Dei]] [[6:3|which is|quæ est]], that is, ought to be, or whose place is, [[6:3|in Jerusalem|in Jerusalem]], [[6:3|should be built|ædificaretur]] [[6:3|in the place where they may offer sacrifices|in loco ubi immolent hostias]], [[6:3|and that they lay the foundations that may support the height|et ut ponant fundamenta supportantia altitudinem]], that is, the structure of the temple, which will be [[6:3|the height of threescore cubits|sexaginta cubitorum]], [[6:3|and the breadth of threescore cubits|et latitudinem cubitorum sexaginta]]. Some think that *breadth* is taken here improperly for the length of the temple, especially since the breadth of Solomon's temple was only twenty cubits[[3 Kings 6:2||]]. Yet Josephus too reports it as it stands in the text. [[6:4|Three rows of unpolished stones, and so rows of new timber|ordines de lapidibus impolitis tres, et sic ordines de lignis novis]]. This seems to be as it were explained by the words of Josephus, where he says: And let them make three walls of it, namely of the temple, of stone, and one wall of wood from the timber of that province. Further, it can be objected that if this second temple was sixty cubits high, it seems to have been higher than Solomon's temple, which was thirty cubits in height, as we have in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 6:2||]]. And the answer is that Solomon's temple was thirty cubits high up to the first storey, then as many again up to the second storey, and from that to the top it had sixty cubits more in height. Whence its whole height is described in the second book of Paralipomenon, where we have: [[2 Par 3:4|the height was a hundred and twenty cubits|Porro altitudo centum viginti cubitorum erat]].

paras.t: Nunc ergo, Thathanai et qui estis trans fluvium, procul recedite ab illis, scilicet Judæis reædificantibus templum et urbem Jerusalem, et dimittite fieri templum Dei a duce Judæorum. Et offerant oblationes Deo cæli, orentque pro vita regis Darii et filiorum ejus prospere conservanda. Circa hoc scribit quidam: Ex hoc patet, quod rex iste habebat fidem unius veri Dei. Verumtamen, an habuit fidem formatam vel solum informem, an potius solummodo fidem suasam et quamdam credulitatem fidei similem, non autem fidem quæ est theologica virtus, puto incertum. Nam (ut patuit) etiam Samaritani idololatræ, credebant, supplicabant et sacrificabant uni vero Deo. Similiter Assuerus, cujus conjux fuit Esther, credebat esse unum verum et summum Deum, omnium provisorem, ut patet in ejus epistolis, præsertim Esther ultimo. Et tamen isti non habuerunt fidem quæ est virtus theologica, nec formatam neque informem, sicut neque hæretici nec Sarraceni, qui unum Deum, non idola colunt.
paras.en: [[6:6|Now therefore Thathanai|Nunc ergo, Thathanai]], [[6:6|who are beyond the river, depart far from them|et qui estis trans fluvium, procul recedite ab illis]], that is, from the Jews who are rebuilding the temple and the city of Jerusalem, [[6:7|And let that temple of God be built by the governor of the Jews|et dimittite fieri templum Dei a duce Judæorum]]. [[6:10|And let them offer oblations to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king|Et offerant oblationes Deo cæli, orentque pro vita regis]] Darius, [[6:10|and of his children|et filiorum ejus]], that it may be prosperously preserved. On this a certain writer says: From this it is plain that this king had faith in the one true God. Yet whether he had formed faith or only unformed faith, or rather only a persuaded faith and a certain credulity like faith, but not the faith which is a theological virtue, I think is uncertain [formed faith is faith quickened by charity; unformed faith is true faith without charity]. For (as was shown) even the idolatrous Samaritans believed in, prayed to and sacrificed to the one true God[[4 Kings 17:33||]]. Likewise Assuerus, whose wife was Esther, believed that there is one true and supreme God, who provides for all, as is plain in his letters, especially in the last chapter of Esther[[Esth 16:16||]]. And yet these men did not have the faith which is a theological virtue, neither formed nor unformed, just as neither heretics nor Saracens have it, who worship one God and not idols.

paras.t: A me ergo Dario rege positum est decretum, id est ordinatio et præceptum, ut omnis homo qui hanc mutaverit jussionem, id est, transgressus fuerit eam, tollatur lignum de domo ipsius, si habuerit domum et lignum pro patibulo aptum: alioqui aliunde sumatur hujusmodi lignum: et configatur in eo. Domus autem ejus publicetur, id est, facultates ipsius ad fiscum pertineant regis. Deus qui habitare facit nomen suum ibi, id est, qui in templo Jerusalem jussit se invocari, nominari, laudari, et qui se ipsum voluit ibi per specialem gratiam esse et habitare, dissipet omnia regna, et populum qui extenderit manum suam ut repugnet, et dissipet domum Dei.
paras.en: [[6:11|And I have made a decree|A me ergo Dario rege positum est decretum]], by me, king Darius, that is, an ordinance and command: [[6:11|That if any whosoever, shall alter this commandment|ut omnis homo qui hanc mutaverit jussionem]], that is, transgress it, [[6:11|a beam be taken from his house|tollatur lignum de domo ipsius]], if he has a house and a beam fit for a gibbet; otherwise let such a beam be taken from elsewhere: [[6:11|and he be nailed upon it|et configatur in eo]]. [[6:11|and his house be confiscated|Domus autem ejus publicetur]], that is, let his goods belong to the king's treasury. [[6:12|And may the God, that hath caused his name to dwell there|Deus qui habitare facit nomen suum ibi]], that is, who commanded that he be called upon, named and praised in the temple of Jerusalem, and who willed himself to be and to dwell there by special grace, [[6:12|destroy all kingdoms, and the people that shall put out their hand to resist, and to destroy the house of God|dissipet omnia regna, et populum qui extenderit manum suam ut repugnet, et dissipet domum Dei]].

paras.t: Ædificaverunt Judæi templum et urbem, jubente Deo per Aggeum et Zachariam prophetas, et jubente Cyro et Dario et Artaxerxe regibus Persarum; et compleverunt domum Dei. Ex qua forma verborum patet falsitas Rabbi Salomonis, dicentis quod Artaxerxes iste fuit idem qui Darius: quod si verum esset, Scriptura non loqueretur de eo et Dario cum interpositione hujusmodi conjunctionis copulativæ. Idcirco cum Josepho dicendum, quod Artaxerxes ille fuit filius Darii, et a Josepho Xerxes vocatur. Nec obstat, quod templum dicitur esse completum sexto Darii anno, videlicet quoad ædificium ejus secundum se: multa tamen deerant ejus ornatui et utensilibus et ædibus in gyro fiendis pro templi ministris. Usque ad diem tertium mensis Adar, qui duodecimus mensis est apud Judæos.
paras.en: The Jews built the temple and the city[[6:14||]], [[6:14|by the commandment of the God of Israel|jubente Deo]] through the prophets Aggeus and Zacharias[[Agg 1:1||]][[Zach 1:1||]][[Zach 4:9||]], [[6:14|and by the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes kings of the Persians|et jubente Cyro et Dario et Artaxerxe regibus Persarum]][[1 Esd 1:3||]][[2 Esd 2:8||]]; [[6:15|And they were finishing this house of God|et compleverunt domum Dei]]. From this form of words the falsity of Rabbi Solomon is plain, who says that this Artaxerxes was the same as Darius: for if that were true, Scripture would not speak of him and of Darius with such a copulative conjunction set between them. Therefore it must be said with Josephus that that Artaxerxes was the son of Darius, and is called Xerxes by Josephus. Nor is it any objection that the temple is said to have been completed in the sixth year of Darius, namely as to its building in itself: yet much was still lacking to its adornment and furnishings and to the dwellings to be made round about it for the ministers of the temple. [[6:15|until the third day of the month of Adar|Usque ad diem tertium mensis Adar]], which is the twelfth month among the Jews.

paras.t: Deinde in littera describitur, qualiter Judæi seu filii transmigrationis, id est de transmigratione et captivitate reversi, fecerunt dedicationem templi; et pontifex ac majores fecerunt sacerdotes ac Levitas stare ordinate secundum congruentiam officiorum suorum in vicibus suis, in quibus ministrare debebant et exercere opera Dei, sacrificando, laudando, et circa hostias præparandas ministerium exhibendo, sicut scriptum est in libro Moysis, præsertim in Levitico et libro Numerorum per diversa capitula: et plana est littera.
paras.en: Then the text describes how the Jews, or [[6:16|the children of the captivity|filii transmigrationis]], that is, those returned from the transmigration and captivity, [[6:16|kept the dedication|fecerunt dedicationem]] of the temple; and the high priest and the elders made the priests and Levites stand in order, according to the fitness of their offices, [[6:18|in their courses|in vicibus suis]], in which they were to minister and to do [[6:18|the works of God|opera Dei]], by sacrificing, by praising, and by serving about the preparing of the victims, [[6:18|as it is written in the book of Moses|sicut scriptum est in libro Moysis]], especially in Leviticus and in the book of Numbers, in various chapters: and the text is plain.

paras.t: Et purificati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ, id est, ad faciendum pascha secundum legem erant dispositi et purgati per orationes, lotiones et continentiam, atque per immunitatem ab irregularitatibus et immunditiis legis, a quibus debebant esse immunes aut purgati pascha facturi et agnum paschalem manducaturi: de quibus omnibus in Exodo, Levitico et ceteris Moysis libris diffuse tractatur. Purificati sunt ergo quasi vir unus, id est omnes concorditer sine exceptione. Et fecerunt solennitatem Azymorum septem diebus in lætitia, quoniam lætificaverat eos Dominus, gratiose agendo cum ipsis, et converterat cor regis Assur ad eos, ut adjuvaret manus eorum, id est, mentem Darii regis inclinaverat ad faciendum tam liberaliter et benigne cum ipsis, et ad habendum se tam devote circa Deum et templum. Dicitur autem Darius rex Persarum, rex Assur, quia et regnum Assyriorum fuit sub ejus imperio.
paras.en: [[6:20|For all the priests and the Levites were purified|Et purificati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ]], that is, to keep the pasch according to the law they were prepared and cleansed by prayers, washings and continence, and by freedom from the irregularities and uncleannesses of the law, from which those who were to keep the pasch and eat the paschal lamb had to be free or cleansed: of all which Exodus, Leviticus and the other books of Moses treat at length. So they were purified [[6:20|as one man|quasi vir unus]], that is, all with one accord, without exception. [[6:22|And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy, for the Lord had made them joyful|Et fecerunt solennitatem Azymorum septem diebus in lætitia, quoniam lætificaverat eos Dominus]], dealing graciously with them, [[6:22|and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them, that he should help their hands|et converterat cor regis Assur ad eos, ut adjuvaret manus eorum]], that is, he had inclined the mind of king Darius to deal so freely and kindly with them, and to bear himself so devoutly towards God and the temple. And Darius, king of the Persians, is called king of Assyria because the kingdom of the Assyrians too was under his rule.

7.title: Elucidatio capituli septimi: Post hæc autem verba
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: Now after these things

paras.t: Recitatur hic promotio atque prosperitas Judæorum sub filio Darii regis.
paras.en: Here is related the advancement and prosperity of the Jews under the son of king Darius.

paras.t: Post hæc autem verba, id est post gesta jam ante descripta sub Dario. Sæpe autem in Scripturis sumitur verbum pro re significata per verbum. In regno Artaxerxis, videlicet filii Darii, quem Artaxerxem Josephus vocat Xerxem, Esdras, cujus genealogia in textu describitur, ascendendo usque ad Aaron, qui fuit sacerdos ab initio, id est pontifex Judæorum primus, a tempore quo Deus per Moysen in deserto instituit sacerdotium Judæorum, distinctum a sacerdotio legis naturalis, in qua omnes primogeniti fuerant sacerdotes. Fuerunt tamen plures intermedii inter Esdram et Aaron, quam hic exprimuntur, sicut ex primo Paralipomenon libro elicitur: principaliores autem ponuntur hic.
paras.en: [[7:1|Now after these things|Post hæc autem verba]], that is, after the deeds already described under Darius; for in the Scriptures *word* [*verbum*] is often taken for the thing signified by the word. [[7:1|in the reign of Artaxerxes|In regno Artaxerxis]], namely the son of Darius, whom Josephus calls Xerxes, [[7:1|Esdras|Esdras]], whose genealogy is described in the text, going up as far as [[7:5|Aaron, the priest from the beginning|Aaron, qui fuit sacerdos ab initio]], that is, the first high priest of the Jews, from the time when God through Moses in the desert instituted the priesthood of the Jews[[Ex 28:1||]], distinct from the priesthood of the natural law, in which all the first-born had been priests. Yet there were more between Esdras and Aaron than are named here, as can be gathered from the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 6:3||]]: but the chief of them are set down here.

paras.t: Ipse Esdras ascendit de Babylone versus Judæam, quæ in altiori est situ, quam Babyloniæ terra. Dicunt autem nonnulli, quod Esdras primo ascenderat cum Zorobabel, deinde Babyloniam rediit ad deducendum secum plures inde in Judæam, et ad impetrandum privilegia quædam a rege. Quod si ita est, mirum quod non fit de eo mentio specialis in descriptione reversionis Zorobabel. Ex Josepho quoque et ex Scholastica historia id non apparet. Et ipse scriba velox in lege Moysis, id est doctus valde et peritus in Scripturis veteris Testamenti: qui et ideo dicitur, scriba velox, quoniam novos apices litterarum excogitavit faciliores ad scribendum et exprimendum; qui et legem a Chaldæis combustam dicitur reparasse, et ceteras veteris Testamenti Scripturas recuperasse. Pentateuchum vero, id est libros Moysis, apud Samaritanos invenisse asseritur. Et dedit ei rex Artaxerxes secundum manum Domini Dei ejus super eum bonam, id est secundum gratiosam et potentem opem et adsistentiam Dei, omnem petitionem ejus, id est, universa quæ a præfato petiit rege. De hoc Josephus undecimo Antiquitatum recitat libro: Fuit in Babylone vir justus et gloria magna potitus, apud multitudinem primus populi Judæorum sacerdos, qui quum legum Moysis integram haberet scientiam, amicus factus est Xerxi regi. Præterea advertendum, quod secundum Magistrum in historiis, Artaxerxes iste fuit alter quam Xerxes filius Darii, et successit in regno Xerxi præfato, atque vocatus est Artaxerxes Longimanus.
paras.en: [[7:6|This Esdras went up from Babylon|Ipse Esdras ascendit de Babylone]] towards Judea, which lies higher than the land of Babylonia. Some say that Esdras had first gone up with Zorobabel, then returned to Babylonia to bring more people from there with him into Judea and to obtain certain privileges from the king. If that is so, it is strange that no special mention is made of him in the account of the return under Zorobabel; nor does it appear from Josephus or from the Scholastic History. [[7:6|and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses|Et ipse scriba velox in lege Moysis]], that is, very learned and skilled in the Scriptures of the Old Testament; and he is called *a ready scribe* [*scriba velox*, "a swift scribe"] because he devised new forms of letters, easier for writing and expressing; he is also said to have restored the law burnt by the Chaldeans and to have recovered the other Scriptures of the Old Testament, and he is asserted to have found the Pentateuch, that is, the books of Moses, among the Samaritans. [[7:6|and the king granted him|Et dedit ei rex]] Artaxerxes, [[7:6|according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him|secundum manum Domini Dei ejus super eum]], a good hand[[7:9||]], that is, according to the gracious and mighty help and assistance of God, [[7:6|all his request|omnem petitionem ejus]], that is, all that he asked of the said king. Of this Josephus tells in the eleventh book of the Antiquities: There was in Babylon a just man who had won great glory, first priest of the people of the Jews among the multitude, who, since he had full knowledge of the laws of Moses, became a friend of king Xerxes. Note further that according to the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor] this Artaxerxes was another than Xerxes the son of Darius, and succeeded the said Xerxes in the kingdom, and was called Artaxerxes Longimanus.

paras.t: Esdras autem paravit, id est, aptavit et præbuit, cor suum ut investigaret legem Domini, id est, eam recoleret et recuperaret, et faceret, id est, obediret eidem: quia scientia præceptorum et legum ordinatur ad opus, quemadmodum et Philosophus protestatur, Quid sit virtus scrutamur, ut boni efficiamur. Ideo scienti et non facienti, peccatum est illi. Et doceret in Israel præceptum et judicium, id est, ipsum Israeliticum populum reversum doceret per verba et scripta præcepta moralia, puta Decalogum et mandata judicialia, quæ assignant modum servandi justitiam inter proximos. Per hæc autem insinuatur, quod docuit quoque præcepta cærimonialia, quæ docent modum colendi Deum in sacrificiis, et in discretione ciborum, ac consimilium rerum figuralium.
paras.en: [[7:10|For Esdras had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord|Esdras enim paravit cor suum, ut investigaret legem Domini]], *prepared*, that is, fitted and offered; *to seek*, that is, to study it again and recover it; [[7:10|and to do|et faceret]], that is, to obey it: because the knowledge of precepts and laws is ordered to doing, as the Philosopher too declares: We inquire what virtue is in order to become good. Therefore, to him [[Jas 4:17|who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|scienti et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]. [[7:10|and to teach in Israel the commandments and judgment|Et doceret in Israel præceptum et judicium]], that is, that he might teach the returned people of Israel by word and writing the moral precepts, such as the Decalogue, and the judicial commandments, which set out the way of keeping justice between neighbours. And by this it is suggested that he taught the ceremonial precepts too, which teach the way of worshipping God in sacrifices, in the distinction of foods, and in like figurative things.

paras.t: Hoc est autem exemplar epistolæ contentivæ edicti, id est præcepti seu ordinationis, quod dedit rex Artaxerxes Esdræ sacerdoti: Artaxerxes rex regum terrenorum subjectorum monarchiæ Persarum, Esdræ doctissimo salutem. Nam et propter sapientiam suam, Esdras fuit regi tam acceptus, carus, et honoratus ab ipso. Atque, ut refert Hieronymus, Hebræi dicunt ipsum fuisse Malachiam prophetam, qui inter duodecim Prophetas est ultimus, et fuisse eum adspectus angelici, et sic erat decorus et multum amabilis.
paras.en: [[7:11|And this is the copy of the letter of the edict|Hoc est autem exemplar epistolæ contentivæ edicti]], that is, the letter containing the edict, that is, the command or ordinance, [[7:11|which king Artaxerxes gave to Esdras the priest|quod dedit rex Artaxerxes Esdræ sacerdoti]]: [[7:12|Artaxerxes king of kings|Artaxerxes rex regum]], of the earthly kings subject to the monarchy of the Persians, [[7:12|to Esdras|Esdræ]] [[7:12|the most learned|doctissimo]] [[7:12|greeting|salutem]]. For because of his wisdom Esdras was so acceptable and dear to the king and so honoured by him. And, as Jerome relates, the Hebrews say that he was the prophet Malachias, who is the last among the twelve Prophets, and that he was of angelic aspect, and so was comely and much to be loved.

paras.t: A me decretum est, ut cuicumque placuerit in regno meo, id est toto imperio meo, de populo Israel, tecum vadat in Jerusalem. A facie enim regis et septem consiliatorum ejus, id est a persona ac præsentia mea et septem principalium consiliariorum meorum, missus es. Nempe, ut legitur in libro Esther, reges Persarum et Medorum habebant assidue secum septem nobilissimos duces in jure et legibus peritissimos, quorum consilio cuncta agebant. Ut visites Judæam et Jerusalem, id est terram et populum tuum, in lege Dei tui, id est cum observantia et memoria legis Mosaicæ, quæ est in manu, id est operatione tua, id est, quam habes ad manum, hoc est in promptu; et ut feras, id est, tecum portes, argentum et aurum, quod rex et consiliatores ejus sponte obtulerunt Deo Israel in subsidium ornamentorum, sacrificiorum ac ædium templi. Jam itaque notitia veri Dei longe ac late innotuit gentibus ex dispersione et commoratione filiorum Israel inter illos, et ex perpetratione mirabilium quæ Deus tunc fecit inter gentiles illis temporibus; ex relatione quoque Israelitarum narrantium gentibus magnalia Dei scripta in lege. Et hæc fuit una causa, cur Deus punivit peccata populi sui per dispersionem inter gentiles. Propter quod scriptum est in libro Tobiæ: Confitemini Domino, filii Israel, et in conspectu gentium laudate eum: quoniam ideo dispersit vos inter gentes quæ ignorant Deum, ut enarretis mirabilia ejus, et faciatis scire eos, quoniam non est alius Deus omnipotens præter eum.
paras.en: [[7:13|It is decreed by me|A me decretum est]] that whoever is minded, [[7:13|in my realm|in regno meo]], that is, in my whole empire, [[7:13|of the people of Israel|de populo Israel]], [[7:13|to go into Jerusalem, should go with thee|tecum vadat in Jerusalem]]. [[7:14|For thou art sent from before the king, and his seven counsellors|A facie enim regis, et septem consiliatorum ejus, missus es]], that is, from my person and presence and that of my seven chief counsellors. For, as we read in the book of Esther, the kings of the Persians and Medes always had with them seven most noble princes, most skilled in right and laws, by whose counsel they did all things[[Esth 1:13||]][[Esth 1:14||]]. [[7:14|to visit Judea and Jerusalem|Ut visites Judæam et Jerusalem]], that is, thy land and people, [[7:14|according to the law of thy God|in lege Dei tui]], that is, with the observance and remembrance of the law of Moses, [[7:14|which is in thy hand|quæ est in manu]], that is, in thy working, or which thou hast at hand, that is, ready; [[7:15|And to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the God of Israel|et ut feras, id est, tecum portes, argentum et aurum, quod rex et consiliatores ejus sponte obtulerunt Deo Israel]] (*to carry*, that is, to take with thee) for the help of the adornments, sacrifices and buildings of the temple. So by now the knowledge of the true God had become known far and wide among the gentiles, from the dispersion of the children of Israel and their dwelling among them, from the wonders which God then wrought among the gentiles in those times, and also from the Israelites telling the gentiles of the great works of God written in the law. And this was one reason why God punished the sins of his people by dispersion among the gentiles. For which reason it is written in the book of Tobias: [[Tob 13:3|Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles|Confitemini Domino, filii Israel, et in conspectu gentium laudate eum]]: [[Tob 13:4|Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, that you may declare his wonderful works, and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him|quoniam ideo dispersit vos inter gentes quæ ignorant Deum, ut enarretis mirabilia ejus, et faciatis scire eos, quoniam non est alius Deus omnipotens præter eum]].

paras.t: Et omne argentum et aurum quodcumque inveneris in universa provincia Babylonis, et quod populus offerre voluerit, id est populus tuus residuus, qui non vult tecum ascendere in Judam, detentus amore uxorum ac sobolis ac possessionum, quas habet in Babylone; vel, populus meus residuus post me et septem consiliarios meos. Vasa quoque quæ dantur in ministerium domus Dei tui, id est sacra vasa deputata ad Dei cultum in templo, trade in conspectu Dei, id est, in templo repone tempore opportuno.
paras.en: [[7:16|And all the silver and gold that thou shalt find in all the province of Babylon, and that the people is willing to offer|Et omne argentum et aurum quodcumque inveneris in universa provincia Babylonis, et quod populus offerre voluerit]], that is, the rest of thy people, who will not go up with thee into Juda, held back by love of their wives and offspring and of the possessions they have in Babylon; or, the rest of my people, after me and my seven counsellors. [[7:19|The vessels also, that are given thee for the sacrifice of the house of thy God|Vasa quoque quæ dantur in ministerium domus Dei tui]], that is, the sacred vessels set apart for the worship of God in the temple, [[7:19|deliver thou in the sight of God|trade in conspectu Dei]], that is, lay them up in the temple at the fitting time.

paras.t: Sed et cetera quibus opus fuerit in domo Dei tui, dabis de thesauro et de fisco regis, id est, emes de pecunia ad me pertinente, quam accipies a præfectis meis trans flumen. Itaque, De fisco, id est de communi pecunia, seu camera regis. Ego Artaxerxes rex statui, id est jussi et commisi omnibus custodibus arcæ publicæ, id est repositoriorum pecuniæ meæ seu thesaurizariis meis, ut quodcumque petierit Esdras a vobis, absque mora detis ei usque ad argenti talenta centum, et usque centum batos vini. Batus mensura est, quæ alio nomine dicitur ephi, videlicet trium modiorum. Et usque ad frumenti coros centum. Corus hic sumitur pro mensura aridorum, sicut batus pro mensura liquidorum. Et continet corus, ut legitur, decem modios. Estque tertia pars oneris quod potest portare camelus. Verumtamen mensuræ istæ apud diversos valde diversificantur, nec scire valemus de facili certam quantitatem earum.
paras.en: [[7:20|And whatsoever more there shall be need of for the house of thy God|Sed et cetera quibus opus fuerit in domo Dei tui]], [[7:20|it shall be given out of the treasury, and the king's exchequer|dabis de thesauro et de fisco regis]], that is, thou shalt buy with money belonging to me, which thou shalt receive from my governors beyond the river. And so: *out of the exchequer*, that is, of the common money, or the king's chamber. [[7:21|I Artaxerxes the king have ordered and decreed to all the keepers of the public chest|Ego Artaxerxes rex statui, id est jussi et commisi omnibus custodibus arcæ publicæ]], that is, of the storehouses of my money, or my treasurers, [[7:21|that whatsoever Esdras|ut quodcumque petierit Esdras]] [[7:21|shall require of you, you give it without delay|a vobis, absque mora detis ei]], [[7:22|Unto a hundred talents of silver|usque ad argenti talenta centum]], [[7:22|and unto a hundred bates of wine|et usque centum batos vini]]. A bate is a measure which by another name is called an ephi[[Ezech 45:11||]], namely of three modii. [[7:22|and unto a hundred cores of wheat|Et usque ad frumenti coros centum]]. A core is taken here for a measure of dry things, as a bate for a measure of liquids. And a core contains, as we read, ten modii; and it is the third part of the load a camel can carry. Yet these measures vary greatly among different peoples, nor can we easily know their exact quantity.

paras.t: Tu autem, Esdra, secundum sapientiam Dei tui, quæ est in manu tua, id est juxta sapientiam tibi a Deo collatam, constitue judices et præsides, ut judicent omni populo qui est trans flumen, id est, provide ut ibi sint judices et præsidentes idonei, prudentes, qui ad profectum populi judicent recte in omni causa, quia potestatem habes instituendi tales, et destituendi indignos; his videlicet qui noverunt legem Dei tui, id est, qui judicent peritis in lege tua, videlicet populo tuo: et ita videtur potestas ista extendi ad judices et præsides præficiendos Judæis, et forsan ex plebe eorum.
paras.en: [[7:25|And thou Esdras according to the wisdom of thy God, which is in thy hand|Tu autem, Esdra, secundum sapientiam Dei tui, quæ est in manu tua]], that is, according to the wisdom bestowed on thee by God, [[7:25|appoint judges and magistrates, that may judge all the people, that is beyond the river|constitue judices et præsides, ut judicent omni populo qui est trans flumen]], that is, provide that there be fit and prudent judges and rulers there, who may judge rightly in every cause for the good of the people, since thou hast power to appoint such and to remove the unworthy; [[7:25|for them who know the law of thy God|his videlicet qui noverunt legem Dei tui]], that is, who may judge those skilled in thy law, namely thy people: and so this power seems to extend to setting judges and rulers over the Jews, and perhaps from among their own people.

paras.t: Et omnis Judæus natione vel conversione ad Judaismum, qui non fecerit legem Dei tui, et legem regis, id est præcepta mea, diligenter, judicium erit de eo, sive in mortem, sive in exsilium, sive in condemnationem substantiæ, vel certe in carcerem: id est, volo ut talis adjudicetur morti corporali aut exsilio, quod est mors civilis, aut privationi possessionum suarum in toto aut parte, seu incarcerationi secundum exigentiam gravitatis aut parvitatis sui excessus, vel secundum quod peccatum ejus processerit ex ignorantia, aut infirmitate, vel ex certa malitia.
paras.en: [[7:26|And whosoever|Et omnis]] Jew, by birth or by conversion to Judaism, [[7:26|will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king|qui non fecerit legem Dei tui, et legem regis]], that is, my commands, [[7:26|diligently, judgment shall be executed upon him, either unto death, or unto banishment, or to the confiscation of goods, or at least to prison|diligenter, judicium erit de eo, sive in mortem, sive in exsilium, sive in condemnationem substantiæ, vel certe in carcerem]]: that is, I will that such a man be sentenced to bodily death, or to exile, which is a civil death, or to the loss of his possessions in whole or in part, or to imprisonment, according as the gravity or slightness of his offence requires, or according as his sin proceeded from ignorance, or weakness, or deliberate malice.

paras.t: Et dixit Esdras. Hoc tamen non est de textu, sed subintelligitur. Dixit itaque Esdras, Deo gratias agens, cum jucunditate et admiratione, eo quod Deus omnipotens mentem regis gentilis taliter inclinavit ad promovendum cultum Dei Israel in templo Jerusalem: Benedictus Deus patrum nostrorum, qui dedit hoc in corde regis, ut glorificaret domum Domini, et in me inclinavit misericordiam suam coram rege, id est, pietatem et gratiam suam mihi impendit, per quam fui regi et consiliariis ejus acceptus, atque ab eis in omnibus exauditus. Et ego confortatus manu Dei quæ erat in me, id est divino subsidio, directione et adsistentia Dei corroboratus, congregavi de Israel principes, id est præcipuos quosdam de Judæis adhuc in Babylonia commorantes, qui ascenderent mecum in Jerusalem: quibus monstravi epistolam regis; qua visa, animati fuerunt mecum ascendere.
paras.en: And Esdras said. This however is not in the text, but is understood. So Esdras said, giving thanks to God with gladness and wonder that almighty God had so inclined the mind of a gentile king to promote the worship of the God of Israel in the temple of Jerusalem: [[7:27|Blessed be the Lord the God of our fathers, who hath put this in the king's heart, to glorify the house of the Lord|Benedictus Deus patrum nostrorum, qui dedit hoc in corde regis, ut glorificaret domum Domini]], [[7:28|And hath inclined his mercy toward me before the king|et in me inclinavit misericordiam suam coram rege]], that is, he bestowed his kindness and grace on me, by which I was acceptable to the king and his counsellors and heard by them in all things. [[7:28|and I being strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God, which was upon me|Et ego confortatus manu Dei quæ erat in me]], that is, strengthened by God's help, guidance and assistance, [[7:28|gathered together out of Israel chief men|congregavi de Israel principes]], that is, certain leading men of the Jews still living in Babylonia, [[7:28|to go up with me|qui ascenderent mecum in Jerusalem]] to Jerusalem: to whom I showed the king's letter; and having seen it, they were encouraged to go up with me.

8.title: Expositio capituli octavi: Hi sunt ergo principes familiarum
8.title_en: Exposition of the eighth chapter: Now these are the chief of families

paras.t: Qualiter Esdras cum suis in Jerusalem venerit, hic refertur. Nec est difficultas in littera.
paras.en: Here is related how Esdras came with his company to Jerusalem. Nor is there any difficulty in the letter.

paras.t: Hi sunt ergo principes familiarum, qui ascenderunt mecum in regno Artaxerxis regis: De filiis Phinees, Gerson; de filiis Ithamar, Daniel. Isti fuerunt sacerdotes nati ex Aaron et præfatis filiis ejus, ut catholici expositores fatentur. Ideo quidam inepte circa hoc reprehendit expositores catholicos.
paras.en: [[8:1|Now these are the chief of families|Hi sunt ergo principes familiarum]], [[8:1|who came up with me|qui ascenderunt mecum]] [[8:1|in the reign of Artaxerxes the king|in regno Artaxerxis regis]]: [[8:2|Of the sons of Phinees, Gersom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel|De filiis Phinees, Gerson; de filiis Ithamar, Daniel]] These were priests born of Aaron and of his sons named here, as the catholic expositors maintain. So a certain writer finds fault with the catholic expositors on this point to no purpose.

paras.t: Congregavi autem eos ad fluvium, qui decurrit ad Ahava. Josephus dicit, Ad Euphraten: et forsan venerunt ad aliquem rivum ipsius, seu tandem ad fluvium ipsum. Mansimus diebus tribus, repausando, seu aliquos exspectando, aut de necessariis providendo. Quæsivique in populo et in sacerdotibus de filiis Levi, id est Levitas quosdam, secundum quod Levitæ a sacerdotibus distinguuntur, et inferiores sunt, sacerdotibusque deserviunt, prout in libro Numerorum legitur, et consequenter ibidem capitulo quarto, et non inveni ibi, id est, nullum Levitam reperi ibi mecum.
paras.en: [[8:15|And I gathered them together to the river, which runneth down to Ahava|Congregavi autem eos ad fluvium, qui decurrit ad Ahava]]. Josephus says, To the Euphrates: and perhaps they came to some stream of it, or at last to the river itself. [[8:15|we stayed there three days|Mansimus diebus tribus]], resting, or waiting for some, or providing what was needed. [[8:15|and I sought among the people and among the priests for the sons of Levi|Quæsivique in populo et in sacerdotibus de filiis Levi]], that is, for some Levites, in the sense in which the Levites are distinguished from the priests, and are lower, and serve the priests, as is read in the book of Numbers[[Num 3:6||]], and following on from that, in the fourth chapter there[[Num 4:1||]] [the margin gives Num. iii and following, and iv; no verses are printed], [[8:15|and found none there|et non inveni ibi]], that is, I found no Levite there with me.

paras.t: Itaque misi Eliezer et Ariel et Semeiam et Elnathan et Jarib, etc., ad Eddo, qui est primus in Chaspiæ loco, ut adducerent nobis inde ministros Dei nostri, præsertim Levitas.
paras.en: [[8:16|So I sent Eliezer, and Ariel, and Semeias, and Elnathan, and Jarib|Itaque misi Eliezer et Ariel et Semeiam et Elnathan et Jarib]], etc., [[8:17|to Eddo, who is chief in the place of Chasphia|ad Eddo, qui est primus in Chaspiæ loco]], [[8:17|that they should bring us|ut adducerent nobis]] from there [[8:17|ministers of the house of our God|ministros Dei nostri]], especially Levites.

paras.t: Circa hæc scribit quidam: Dicunt expositores nostri communiter, quod Esdras misit nuntios ad Judæos, qui erant ultra montes Chaspios, quos transtulerant reges Assyriorum. Quod dictum reprobat ille, quia sacerdotes et Levitæ non fuerunt capti cum decem tribubus, quæ sunt ultra Chaspios montes. Nec illi de montibus illis potuissent tam cito venire ad Esdram, sicut in littera venisse dicuntur hi, pro quibus misit. Sed argumenta hæc modici sunt vigoris. Quamvis enim sacerdotes et Levitæ fuerunt capti a Chaldæis diu post decem tribuum captivitatem ab Assyriis, interim tamen durante per septuaginta annos captivitate, et Babylone destructa, poterant quidam de sacerdotibus et Levitis ad decem tribus transisse. Denique decem tribus illæ nondum fuerunt clausæ (Alexander enim rex eas reclusit), atque ut Josephus narrat, erant in Media, id est in regno Medorum: et sic poterant satis cito venire ad Esdram, quia habuerunt a rege licentiam.
paras.en: On these words a certain writer says: Our expositors commonly say that Esdras sent messengers to the Jews who were beyond the Caspian mountains, whom the kings of the Assyrians had carried away. This saying he rejects, because the priests and Levites were not taken captive with the ten tribes, which are beyond the Caspian mountains. Nor could those men have come from those mountains so quickly to Esdras as those for whom he sent are said in the letter to have come. But these arguments are of little force. For although the priests and Levites were taken captive by the Chaldeans long after the captivity of the ten tribes by the Assyrians, yet in the meantime, while the captivity lasted for seventy years, and after Babylon was destroyed, some of the priests and Levites could have gone over to the ten tribes. Moreover those ten tribes were not yet shut in (for king Alexander shut them in), and, as Josephus relates, they were in Media, that is, in the kingdom of the Medes: and so they could come to Esdras quickly enough, since they had leave from the king.

paras.t: Insuper, dictum illud Catholicorum, quod et in Scholastica historia continetur, verbis Josephi consonare videtur, qui ait undecimo libro Antiquitatum: Exemplum epistolæ misit Esdras ad omnes Israelitas et ad Mediam inhabitantes. Ecce manifesta probatio. Additque Josephus: Totus autem populus Israel, scilicet decem tribus, in terra illa permansit. Ideoque duæ tantum tribus sunt constitutæ per Europam et Asiam, obsequentes Romanis. Verumtamen duabus tribubus illis, videlicet Juda et Benjamin, annumeratur tribus Levitica. Atque, ut dictum est sæpe, aliqui ex decem tribubus fuerunt capti cum populo regni Juda, et redierunt vel ipsi vel eorum posteri cum Judæis a Babylone. Asserit etiam Josephus: Decem tribus hactenus trans Euphraten commorari probantur, quarum multitudines innumerabiles numero comprehendi non possunt. De quibus in Scholastica historia additur, quod circa finem mundi egredientur, magnam hominum stragem facturi.
paras.en: Besides, that saying of the Catholics, which is also contained in the Scholastic History, seems to agree with the words of Josephus, who says in the eleventh book of the Antiquities: Esdras sent a copy of the letter to all the Israelites, and to those dwelling in Media. Here is a plain proof. And Josephus adds: But the whole people of Israel, that is, the ten tribes, remained in that land. And so only two tribes were settled through Europe and Asia, subject to the Romans. Yet the tribe of Levi is counted with those two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin. And, as has often been said, some of the ten tribes were taken captive with the people of the kingdom of Juda, and either they themselves or their descendants returned with the Jews from Babylon. Josephus also asserts: The ten tribes are found to dwell beyond the Euphrates to this day, countless multitudes that cannot be numbered. Of them it is added in the Scholastic History that they will come forth about the end of the world, to make a great slaughter of men.

paras.t: Et prædicavi ibi jejunium, hortando ut jejunarent, quatenus Deus custodiret nos in processu itineris. Erubui enim a rege petere auxilium, quia dixeramus regi: Manus, id est protectio, Dei nostri est super omnes qui quærunt eum in bonitate, id est in sinceritate virtutum; et furor, id est rigor suæ justitiæ et vindictæ, incumbit super omnes qui derelinquunt eum. Idcirco ne rex scandalizaretur, si Esdras videretur de divina defensione diffidere quærendo humanum auxilium, Esdras erubuit petere subsidium a rege pro deductione per viam: nec hoc fuit Deum tentare, præsertim quia ex rationabili causa processit, et per orationes atque jejunia ad Deum confugerunt, tam Esdras quam populus ejus.
paras.en: [[8:21|And I proclaimed there a fast|Et prædicavi ibi jejunium]], urging them to fast, so that God might guard us on the way. [[8:22|For I was ashamed to ask the king for aid|Erubui enim a rege petere auxilium]], [[8:22|because we had said to the king|quia dixeramus regi]]: [[8:22|The hand|Manus]], that is, the protection, [[8:22|of our God is upon all them that seek him in goodness|Dei nostri est super omnes qui quærunt eum in bonitate]], that is, in the sincerity of the virtues; [[8:22|and wrath|et furor]], that is, the rigour of his justice and vengeance, lies [[8:22|upon all them that forsake him|super omnes qui derelinquunt eum]]. Therefore, lest the king should be scandalized if Esdras seemed to distrust God's defence by seeking human help, Esdras was ashamed to ask the king for a guard to bring them on their way. Nor was this tempting God, especially since it came from a reasonable cause, and both Esdras and his people took refuge in God by prayers and fasts.

paras.t: Et separavi de principibus sacerdotum duodecim, id est, duodecim notabiliores ex numero sacerdotum elegi. Appendique eis argentum et aurum, et vasa consecrata domus Dei, quæ obtulerat rex et consiliatores ejus, universusque Israel, de numero eorum qui inventi fuerant in terra transmigrationis, nec redierunt: id est, omnia ista assignavi sacerdotibus illis fideliter, sicut ea recepi sub pondere et numero certo. Et crateres aureos, qui sunt vasa duas ansas habentia.
paras.en: [[8:24|And I separated twelve of the chief of the priests|Et separavi de principibus sacerdotum duodecim]], that is, I chose twelve of the more notable out of the number of the priests. [[8:25|And I weighed unto them the silver and gold, and the vessels consecrated for the house of|Appendique eis argentum et aurum, et vasa consecrata domus Dei]] God, [[8:25|which the king and his counsellors|quæ obtulerat rex et consiliatores ejus]] had offered, [[8:25|and all Israel|universusque Israel]], of the number of those [[8:25|that were found|qui inventi fuerant]] in the land of the captivity and did not return: that is, I handed over all these things faithfully to those priests, as I had received them, by a fixed weight and number. [[8:27|And twenty cups of gold|Et crateres aureos]], which are vessels with two handles.

paras.t: Et dixi eis, videlicet sacerdotibus: Vos sancti Domini, id est, vos estis electi ministri Deo consecrati, et vasa hæc sancta sunt. Vigilate et custodite, id est, omnia ista quæ vobis assignavi, et divino sunt cultui deputata, vigilanter custodite, donec appendatis, id est, quousque ea assignetis in Jerusalem, in templo Dei, coram principibus sacerdotum et Levitarum, id est coram principalibus inter sacerdotes atque Levitas. Utensilia namque cultus divini et spiritualia bona, sunt cum præcipua diligentia custodienda.
paras.en: [[8:28|And I said to them|Et dixi eis]], namely to the priests: [[8:28|You are the holy ones of the Lord|Vos sancti Domini]], that is, you are chosen ministers consecrated to God, [[8:28|and the vessels are holy|et vasa hæc sancta sunt]]. [[8:29|Watch ye and keep them|Vigilate et custodite]], that is, watchfully keep all these things which I have handed over to you and which are set apart for divine worship, [[8:29|till you deliver them by weight|donec appendatis]], that is, until you hand them over in Jerusalem, in the temple of God, [[8:29|before the chief of the priests, and of the Levites|coram principibus sacerdotum et Levitarum]], that is, before the chief men among the priests and Levites. For the utensils of divine worship, and spiritual goods, are to be kept with especial care.

paras.t: Promovimus ergo, id est, ad procedendum movimus pedes nostros; et venimus in Jerusalem, et mansimus ibi tribus diebus. Die autem quarta appensum est argentum et aurum et vasa, id est, assignata et tradita sunt in templum, in thesaurum ipsius.
paras.en: [[8:31|Then we set forward|Promovimus ergo]], that is, we moved our feet to go on; [[8:32|And we came to Jerusalem, and we stayed there three days|et venimus in Jerusalem, et mansimus ibi tribus diebus]]. [[8:33|And on the fourth day the silver and the gold, and the vessels were weighed|Die autem quarta appensum est argentum et aurum et vasa]], that is, they were handed over and delivered into the temple, into its treasury.

paras.t: Dederunt autem edicta regis satrapis, id est, epistolam regis Artaxerxis, continentem prætacta præcepta ipsius, præsentaverunt reversi a Babylone, qui erant de conspectu regis, id est ex parte et ex commissione prædicti regis constituti præfecti et duces, trans flumen; et elevaverunt populum et domum Dei, id est, duces ac satrapæ magnifice honoraverunt populum Dei et templum ejus, propter præcepta regis, et propter beneficia ac privilegia quæ rex concessit eisdem.
paras.en: [[8:36|And they gave the king's edicts to the lords|Dederunt autem edicta regis satrapis]], that is, those who had returned from Babylon presented the letter of king Artaxerxes, containing his commands touched on above, to those [[8:36|that were from the king's court|qui erant de conspectu regis]], that is, the governors and leaders appointed on behalf of the said king and by his commission, [[8:36|beyond the river|trans flumen]]; [[8:36|and they furthered the people and the house of God|et elevaverunt populum et domum Dei]], that is, the leaders and lords honoured the people of God and his temple magnificently, because of the king's commands, and because of the benefits and privileges which the king had granted them.

9.title: Expositio capituli noni: Postquam autem hæc completa sunt
9.title_en: Exposition of the ninth chapter: And after these things were accomplished

paras.t: Magna quædam transgressio populi a captivitate reversi, et ejusdem iniquitatis deploratio, hic describuntur.
paras.en: Here are described a great transgression of the people that had returned from the captivity, and the bewailing of that iniquity.

paras.t: Postquam autem hæc, quæ in fine præcedentis capituli enarrantur, completa sunt, accesserunt ad me principes, hoc est aliqui principales et boni de populo illo reverso, dicentes: Non est separatus populus Israel qui cum Zorobabel rediit, a populis terrarum, id est a commixtione gentilium in gyro terræ nostræ morantium.
paras.en: [[9:1|And after these things were accomplished|Postquam autem hæc completa sunt]], the things related at the end of the preceding chapter, [[9:1|the princes came to me|accesserunt ad me principes]], that is, some of the chief and good men of that returned people, [[9:1|saying|dicentes]]: [[9:1|The people of Israel|Non est separatus populus Israel]], who returned with Zorobabel, [[9:1|have not separated themselves from the people of the lands|a populis terrarum]], that is, from mingling with the gentiles dwelling round about our land.

paras.t: Acceperunt enim, id est, acceperunt Judæi, de filiabus eorum sibi et filiis suis uxores, vel potius quasi uxores, quia inter eos, ut infra patebit, non fuit matrimonium verum, et commiscuerunt semen sanctum, id est deputatum ad divinum obsequium, cum populis terrarum, id est cum gentilibus et idololatris. Tamen Judæi qui tantum facinus commiserunt, quamdiu manserunt in illo, non fuerunt sancti, sed vitiosi. Sed in quantum erant specialiter deputati ad cultum Dei, dicuntur sancti: quemadmodum vitiosus prælatus, ratione sacri officii dicitur pater sanctus. Manus etiam principum et magistratuum, id est majorum in populo: non tamen Zorobabel nec pontifex Jesus, ut aliqui dicunt. Hieronymus tamen super Zachariam, ubi fit mentio de hoc Jesu, affirmat eum duxisse uxorem alienigenam. Fuit in transgressione hac prima, id est primo culpabilis, et aliis dans exemplum sic agendi. Tamen quod ait, Prima, posset referri ad transgressionem: ut sit sensus, quod in hac prima transgressione, quæ fuit præcipue gravis, fuerunt culpabiles et ipsi principes magistratusque Judæorum.
paras.en: [[9:2|For they have taken|Acceperunt enim]], that is, the Jews have taken, [[9:2|of their daughters for themselves and for their sons|de filiabus eorum sibi et filiis suis]] wives, or rather wives as it were, since between them, as will be plain further on, there was no true marriage; [[9:2|and they have mingled the holy seed|et commiscuerunt semen sanctum]], that is, the seed set apart for the service of God, [[9:2|with the people of the lands|cum populis terrarum]], that is, with gentiles and idolaters. Yet the Jews who committed so great a crime were not holy, but vicious, as long as they remained in it. But in so far as they were specially set apart for the worship of God they are called holy: as a vicious prelate is called holy father by reason of his sacred office. [[9:2|And the hand of the princes and magistrates|Manus etiam principum et magistratuum]], that is, of the greater men among the people: not however Zorobabel, nor Jesus the high priest, as some say. Yet Jerome on Zacharias, where mention is made of this Jesus[[Zach 3:1||]] [the margin gives Zach. ii; Jesus the high priest appears in Zach 3], affirms that he had married a foreign wife. [[9:2|hath been first in this transgression|Fuit in transgressione hac prima]], that is, guilty first, and giving the others an example of acting so [the words of this lemma are garbled in the OCR and are read with the Vulgate].
