Yet what he says, *first*, could be referred to the transgression: so that the sense is that in this first transgression, which was especially grave, the very princes and magistrates of the Jews were guilty too.

paras.t: Denique, sicut testatur B. Hieronymus super Malachiam, Judæi a Babylone reversi, acceperunt gentiles uxores, repudiatis uxoribus propriis propter earum deformitatem et vetustatem: quod fuit valde dupliciterque enorme, quia et ipsa repudiatio fuit in se vitiosa, et alienigenas ducere, fuit prohibitum in Deuteronomio. Et de hac Judæorum iniquitate agitur Malachiæ secundo, multum sententiose, quamvis breviter et obscure, prout ibi expositum est.
paras.en: Moreover, as blessed Jerome testifies on Malachias, the Jews who returned from Babylon took gentile wives, putting away their own wives because of their plainness and their age: which was doubly and very greatly monstrous, since both the putting away was vicious in itself, and to marry foreign women was forbidden in Deuteronomy[[Deut 7:3||]]. And this iniquity of the Jews is treated in the second chapter of Malachias[[Mal 2:11||]], very pithily, though briefly and obscurely, as has been explained there.

paras.t: Quumque audissem sermonem istum, scidi pallium meum et tunicam, sicut mos fuit Judæorum in magna afflictione et adversitate; et evulsi capillos capitis mei et barbæ, ex vehementi dolore, et in signum mœstitiæ: in quibus apparet fervor dilectionis et zelus justitiæ sancti Esdræ circa Deum et proximos;
paras.en: [[9:3|And when I had heard this word|Quumque audissem sermonem istum]], [[9:3|I rent my mantle and my coat|scidi pallium meum et tunicam]], as was the custom of the Jews in great affliction and adversity; [[9:3|and plucked off the hairs of my head and my beard|et evulsi capillos capitis mei et barbæ]] from vehement grief, and in sign of mourning: in which appear the fervour of charity and the zeal for justice of holy Esdras towards God and his neighbours;

paras.t: et dixi: Deus meus, confundor mente, et erubesco forinsecus, levare faciem meam ad te, id est faciem cordis ad tuam sanctitatem, vel faciem corporalem ad cælum, in quo specialiter esse et habitare cognosceris: et hoc propter enormitatem et fœditatem vitiorum nostrorum, atque ex consideratione puritatis et dignitatis tuæ immensæ. De turpitudine enim et enormitate culparum, summe erubescendum est coram Deo. Hinc subditur: Quoniam iniquitates nostræ commissæ in proximum, multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum, id est in cordibus nostris, et omnino inexcusabiliter imputandæ sunt nobis. Viri enim qui tam scelerata iniere connubia, gravissime peccaverunt in conjuges suas, quas abjecerunt, et eas induxerunt ad magnam desolationem, fletum, pusillanimitatem, et ad multa peccata, scilicet ad iram, murmurationem, impatientiam, invidiam, ad quas passiones pronæ sunt feminæ. Et peccata nostra in Deum commissa, creverunt usque ad cælum, id est, vehementissime multa et gravia sunt effecta. Itaque Esdras ex humilitate connumeravit se transgressoribus illis, sicut et Daniel in sua oratione, et Isaias dum ait de Christo: Nos reputavimus eum quasi leprosum. Et rursus: Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus. Et traditi sumus in gladium et captivitatem et in confusionem vultus, sicut et in die hac: quia et nunc multi insultant nobis, tam hic in Judæa, quam in regnis, ubi fratres nostri sub servitutis jugo morantur.
paras.en: [[9:6|And said: My God I am confounded|et dixi: Deus meus, confundor]] in mind, [[9:6|and ashamed|et erubesco]] outwardly, [[9:6|to lift up my face to thee|levare faciem meam ad te]], that is, the face of my heart to thy holiness, or my bodily face to heaven, where thou art known in a special way to be and to dwell: and this because of the monstrousness and foulness of our vices, and from the thought of thy boundless purity and dignity. For one must blush exceedingly before God at the baseness and monstrousness of one's faults. Hence it is added: [[9:6|for our iniquities|Quoniam iniquitates nostræ]] committed against our neighbour [[9:6|are multiplied over our heads|multiplicatæ sunt super caput nostrum]], that is, in our hearts, and are to be imputed to us with no excuse at all. For the men who entered into such wicked unions sinned most grievously against their wives, whom they cast off, and whom they drove to great desolation, weeping and faintness of heart, and to many sins, namely to anger, murmuring, impatience and envy, passions to which women are prone. [[9:6|and our sins|Et peccata nostra]] committed against God [[9:6|are grown up even unto heaven|creverunt usque ad cælum]], that is, they have become exceedingly many and grave. So Esdras out of humility numbered himself with those transgressors, as Daniel too did in his prayer[[Dan 9:5||]], and Isaias when he says of Christ: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper|Nos reputavimus eum quasi leprosum]]. And again: [[Is 53:6|All we like sheep have gone astray|Omnes nos quasi oves erravimus]]. And we have been [[9:7|delivered|Et traditi sumus]] [[9:7|to the sword, and to captivity|in gladium et captivitatem]], [[9:7|and to confusion of face, as it is at this day|et in confusionem vultus, sicut et in die hac]]: for even now many insult us, both here in Judæa and in the kingdoms where our brethren dwell under the yoke of bondage.

paras.t: Et nunc quasi parum et ad momentum facta est deprecatio nostra ad Dominum Deum nostrum, id est, non nisi modicissimo tempore habuimus idoneitatem deprecandi te, scilicet quamdiu a magnis vitiis eramus immunes, quando eramus in via huc redeundi; et cito postquam huc venimus, tanta commisimus scelera, quod non possumus excusari, nec digni sumus coram te apparere aut deprecari; quia servi sumus regis Persarum, imo et vitiorum. Iniqui namque, teste sacratissimo principe Apostolorum, sunt servi corruptionis. A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est. Et nunc quid dicemus, Domine Deus, post hæc? id est, excusare non possumus nos, qui post tot et tanta beneficia tua tam ingrati fuimus tibi; quia dereliquimus mandata tua, quæ præcepisti in manu, id est per obsequium, servorum tuorum Prophetarum, dicens: Terra ad quam ingredimini, immunda est, scilicet terra promissionis, quæ perhibetur immunda, propter flagitia in ea commissa, et repleverunt eam ab ore usque ad os, per hyperbolen, ad innuendum quod abundantissime ac enormissime in ea peccaverunt Amorrhæi, Chananæi, etc., quorum scelera in Deuteronomio conscribuntur. Sic et Manasses dicitur replesse Jerusalem sanguine innocentium usque ad os.
paras.en: [[9:8|And now as a little, and for a moment has our prayer been made before the Lord our God|Et nunc quasi parum et ad momentum facta est deprecatio nostra ad Dominum Deum nostrum]]: that is, only for the shortest time have we been fit to pray to thee, namely as long as we were free from great vices, while we were on the way back here; and soon after we came here we committed such crimes that we cannot be excused, and are not worthy to appear before thee or to pray to thee; [[9:9|For we are bondmen|quia servi sumus]] of the king of the Persians, nay, and of vices. For the wicked, as the most holy prince of the Apostles testifies, are [[2 Pet 2:19|the slaves of corruption|servi corruptionis]]. [[2 Pet 2:19|For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|A quo enim quis superatus est, hujus et servus est]]. [[9:10|And now, O our God, what shall we say after this?|Et nunc quid dicemus, Domine Deus, post hæc?]] [Denis reads *Domine Deus*, “O Lord God”] That is, we cannot excuse ourselves, who after so many and so great benefits of thine have been so ungrateful to thee; [[9:10|for we have forsaken thy commandments|quia dereliquimus mandata tua]], [[9:11|Which thou hast commanded by the hand|quæ præcepisti in manu]], that is, by the service, [[9:11|of thy servants the prophets, saying|servorum tuorum Prophetarum, dicens]]: [[9:11|The land which you go to possess, is an unclean land|Terra ad quam ingredimini, immunda est]][[Lev 18:25||]], namely the land of promise, which is said to be unclean because of the crimes committed in it, [[9:11|who have filled it from mouth to mouth|et repleverunt eam ab ore usque ad os]]: by hyperbole, to convey that the Amorrhites, the Chanaanites and the rest, whose crimes are set down in Deuteronomy[[Deut 9:4||]][[Deut 18:12||]][[Deut 20:18||]], sinned in it most abundantly and most monstrously. So too Manasses is said to have filled Jerusalem with innocent blood up to the mouth[[4 Kings 21:16||]].

paras.t: Nunc ergo filias vestras ne detis filiis eorum, et filias eorum non accipiatis. Istud præcepit Dominus per Moysen eximium Prophetarum, et per Zachariam ac Malachiam reprehendit hujus præcepti transgressionem. Per aliorum quoque eloquia Prophetarum admonuit populum Israel sæpe de hujus præcepti impletione. Et non quæratis pacem et prosperitatem eorum, id est, non habeatis communionem cum ipsis, sed vitetis omnino eorum consortia: imo Dominus eos occidi jussit, nec ut tales erant amandi. Non tamen fuerant odiendi, quoad personam vel naturam ipsorum. Ut non converteremur ad pristina vitia nostra.
paras.en: [[9:12|Now therefore give not your daughters to their sons|Nunc ergo filias vestras ne detis filiis eorum]], [[9:12|and take not their daughters|et filias eorum non accipiatis]]. This the Lord commanded by Moses, the most excellent of the Prophets[[Deut 7:3||]], and by Zacharias and Malachias[[Mal 2:11||]] He rebuked the transgression of this commandment. By the words of the other Prophets too He often admonished the people of Israel to fulfil this commandment. [[9:12|and seek not their peace, nor their prosperity|Et non quæratis pacem et prosperitatem eorum]], that is, have no communion with them, but shun their company altogether: indeed the Lord commanded them to be slain[[Num 25:17||]][[Num 31:15||]][[Num 31:17||]], nor were they to be loved such as they were. Yet they were not to be hated as regards their person or their nature. [[9:14|That we should not turn away|Ut non converteremur]] to our former vices.

paras.t: Numquid iratus es nobis usque in consummationem? id est, noli, o Domine, noli nos omnino deserere, nec gratiam vitandi peccata totaliter nobis abstrahere, ne penitus pereamus. Domine, Deus Israel, Justus es tu: quoniam derelicti sumus, qui salvaremur, id est, jam pro magna parte propter peccata nostra sumus consumpti, et tamen dereliquisti quosdam residuos, utpote nos, ad hoc ut pœnitendo et bene vivendo consequamur salutem. Ecce coram te sumus in delicto nostro, id est evidenter rei et valde culpabiles. Non enim stari potest coram te super hoc, id est, stare non possumus coram tribunali tuo ad excusandum nos in hac parte: imo si excusare voluerimus nos, os nostrum condemnabit nos; et si voluerimus judicio tecum contendere, non poterimus respondere unum pro mille.
paras.en: [[9:14|Art thou angry with us unto utter destruction|Numquid iratus es nobis usque in consummationem]]? That is, do not, O Lord, do not forsake us altogether, nor wholly withdraw from us the grace of avoiding sins, lest we perish utterly. [[9:15|O Lord God of Israel, thou art just|Domine, Deus Israel, Justus es tu]]: [[9:15|for we remain yet to be saved|quoniam derelicti sumus, qui salvaremur]]: that is, for a great part we have now been consumed because of our sins, and yet thou hast left some remnant, such as us, so that by doing penance and living well we may attain salvation. [[9:15|Behold we are before thee in our sin|Ecce coram te sumus in delicto nostro]], that is, plainly guilty and very blameworthy. [[9:15|for there can be no standing before thee in this matter|Non enim stari potest coram te super hoc]]: that is, we cannot stand before thy judgment seat to excuse ourselves in this matter; nay, if we would excuse ourselves, our own mouth will condemn us[[Job 9:20||]]; and if we would contend with thee in judgment, we shall not be able to answer one for a thousand[[Job 9:3||]].
